data.body:
## Measured classification: 6 classes explain the whole wall, and one is 45% of it

Read-only CI log analysis from macOS. No claim, no transition, no fix.

### The count in the title is an undercount

| Run | Date | Ref | Measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| `35250748887` | 2026-09-17 17:07Z | `4f12815e9a0b` | **1626 failed + 1382 errors = 3008** |
| `35511654149` | 2026-09-20 12:48Z | `e84e4c5e9439` | **1636 failed + 1383 errors = 3019** |

Workflow `294845723` (`Test Suite (mirror)`, `.github/workflows/test.yml`). The count basis is
the final unindented pytest `short test summary info` block, with nested subprocess pytest
summaries excluded so they are not double-counted.

**1626 counted only `FAILED` and missed 1382 `ERROR`s** — setup failures, which is precisely
where the dominant cause lives. The title should say 3008. The 3-day-later run confirms it is
stable and getting marginally worse, not drifting randomly.

### The classes

Percentages are of 3008.

| # | Class | Count | % | Classification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Linked-worktree template copy cannot rewrite `.tickets-tracker\.git` | **1361** | **45.2%** | Cascade from ONE fixture defect |
| 2 | Linux/WSL/POSIX script + process assumptions | 545 | 18.1% | POSIX-only test assumption |
| 3 | Path/newline/encoding + golden-output long tail | 544 | 18.1% | Mostly POSIX-only assumptions |
| 4 | Offline network-guard / mock gaps | 392 | 13.0% | Test-harness defect |
| 5 | OpenSSH op-cert toolchain + Windows ACL semantics | 98 | 3.3% | Runner toolchain gap |
| 6 | MAX_PATH and remaining file-lock defects | 68 | 2.3% | **Genuine portability defect** |

Representative verbatim errors:

```
1: PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied:
   'C:\...\test_half_fixed_copy_is_reject0\half\.tickets-tracker\.git'
2: CalledProcessError: Command '['bash', 'D:\a\rebar\rebar\infra\scripts\vartmp-cap.sh',
   '--print-conf']' returned non-zero exit status 1
3: UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x97 in position 976
4: RuntimeError: Network access is forbidden in unit/scripts tests.
5: SigningError: cannot mint op-cert signature: ssh-keygen (OpenSSH) not found;
   SSHSIG requires OpenSSH >= 8.9
6: SnapshotError: git checkout-index ... error: unable to create file
   C:\...\rebar-gate-snapshots\tmp\tickets-752d00fbe360-...-CREATE.json: Filename too long
```

### The important structural finding

**Class 1 is not 1361 bugs. It is one fixture defect with 1361 dependents.** The per-test store
template copy/rewrite path fails on `.tickets-tracker\.git`, and every interface test that needs
a store then dies at setup. That is why the `ERROR` count is so close to the `FAILED` count and
why counting only `FAILED` was so misleading.

Fixing that one path plausibly takes the wall from 3008 to roughly 1650 in a single change,
without touching any product code. Nothing else on this list has that leverage.

The likely mechanism is a POSIX metadata assumption in the copy/rewrite — on Windows, `.git`
inside the copied template is not rewritable the way the fixture expects, and a linked worktree's
`.git` is a **file** containing a `gitdir:` pointer rather than a directory, which is exactly the
kind of thing that works everywhere on POSIX and not at all on Windows.

### Recommended sequence, by signal recovered per unit of work

1. **Class 1** — one fixture fix, recovers 45% and removes the cascade that is currently hiding
   everything behind it. Do this before diagnosing anything else, because the residual long tail
   cannot be honestly classified until the setup cascade is gone.
2. **Class 2** — decide per test: make portable, or explicitly mark non-Windows. 545 outcomes that
   require `bash`/WSL/`fcntl`/`os.geteuid` are not Windows product signal in any case.
3. **Class 4** — deterministic harness work: mock the provider path or mark genuine loopback tests
   `@pytest.mark.allow_network`. The guard is behaving correctly; the tests are under-mocked.
4. **Class 3** — only tractable after 1, 2 and 4 clear. 438 of it is an undecomposed assertion
   tail that is not worth root-causing while the cascade is still in place.
5. **Class 5** — a scoping call: provision OpenSSH ≥ 8.9 on the runner, or declare op-cert tests
   unsupported on Windows.
6. **Class 6** — small but the only class that is a **real product defect affecting real Windows
   users**. Prefer shortening rebar's constructed paths over enabling `core.longpaths` on the
   runner: runner config hides the defect from CI while leaving it live for downstream users.

### Gate verdict

**Not worth keeping as a gate in its current form.** At ~3000 red outcomes a new regression is
invisible, which is the definition of a destroyed signal. Keep it `continue-on-error` while
classes 1–4 are worked, then either restore it as a gate over a maintained Windows subset, or
enumerate a baseline so it fails only on NEW classes — the same ratchet shape this repo already
uses for module size, complexity and mechanism growth.

### Could not establish

- The 438-outcome residual assertion tail inside class 3 is measured but not decomposed. Doing
  that before removing the class-1 cascade would be low-value.
- Not reproduced on Windows; this is CI log and code analysis from macOS.
- The MAX_PATH policy in class 6 is a deliberate human scoping decision and was not made here.
